title: Khmer Rouge takeover of Cambodia
summary: On 17 April 1975 Khmer Rouge forces led by Pol Pot entered Phnom Penh and ordered the city's roughly two million residents out at gunpoint; thousands died on the crowded roads. The regime ruled until Vietnamese forces ended it in 1979. Ben Kiernan estimates 1.5 to 2 million people were murdered, about a fifth of the population.

where.historical_name: Phnom Penh, capital of Cambodia, held by the government until its fall

importance.justification: Start of a regime whose forced labour, executions and starvation killed a large share of Cambodia's population.

audience_note: Describes a mass atrocity and genocide: forced evacuation at gunpoint, executions, and deaths from starvation and forced labour. Death-toll figures are contested estimates.
